cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, and nothing is decided.
cells.act: remember what drew you and face it again
cells.ask: Recall what drew you toward this before it had a name — a room, a person, a sentence. Sit with it; no decision to make. Just face it again.
cells.core:
You are open right now in a way that usually shows up only at the start of things, and it is not naivety. It is the part of you that holds every option without rushing to pick one, and today that holding is working. You can stand in the middle of it without the ground tilting.

What gets missed when this is steady is what first pulled you. Go back to what drew you in before it had a name — a person, a room, a sentence you read once — and face it again for a minute. Not to decide anything. Just to remember the pull was yours before it was a plan. That is what you are made of.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold every option open and still know what pulls you.
cells.verb: Holding everything open before any of it is chosen
cells.place: In the quiet before you become what you already are

cells.tense: You will be somewhere else by the time any of this lands.
cells.act: stop performing and simply do it
cells.ask: Choose the option you keep circling and do its smallest honest version today, in your own hands, without announcing it to anyone, and without needing to feel ready.
cells.core:
You are hovering. Every door is open and none of them is being walked through, and the longer you stand there the more each option has to be perfect before you touch it. From the outside it looks like you are still deciding. Underneath it feels more like bracing — something might be chosen before you are ready for it.

Nothing lands until something lands. Pick the thing you keep circling and do the smallest honest version of it today, in your own hands, without announcing it. You do not need to feel certain first; certainty is what shows up afterward, or it does not, and either way the thing is done. One real act is worth more than every version still in the air.
cells.sheetLine: One door walked through beats every open one.
cells.verb: Holding everything open before any of it is chosen
cells.place: In the quiet before you become what you already are

cells.tense: You keep standing at a door that already closed behind you.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: Stay with something familiar — a place, a practice, a piece of work — longer than usual, and ask nothing new of it. Let a second layer show itself when it does.
cells.core:
There is an opening in you that shut long enough back that you have stopped noticing the wall. You can still make things — the ability stayed — but they come out tighter than they need to, built close to the edges, made to fit through a narrow space. That is not a lack of talent. It is a room that got smaller than the person standing in it.

Nothing has to be pried open. Stay with something you know well — a place, a practice, a piece of work — and look at it longer than you have before, asking it for nothing new. What is shut does not need forcing. It needs something to keep looking while it decides.
cells.sheetLine: You still make things. You make them small enough to fit.

cells.tense: The pen is down while you are still writing on the page.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Take the next step actually under your feet, with the little light you have. Don't plan the one after it; when this step is done, more ground tends to show.
cells.core:
You are moving faster than you are choosing. Decisions are getting made — something keeps getting done — but not by you in the moment they happen; the reaction arrives and you are already past it. Doors you could not see are not locked. They were not in the picture.

Not every path needs seeing first. Take the next step actually under your feet and do only that one, with the little bit of light you have. Do not plan the step after it. When that one is done, the ground ahead tends to show a little more. You can steer once you can see, and you see by moving.
cells.sheetLine: You can steer only what you can see, and you see by moving.
cells.verb: Holding everything open before any of it is chosen
cells.place: In the quiet before you become what you already are

attempts.check: The Too Little cell is the one where I could overreach: the record says past wounds sealed the opening, but it never says what happened, who, or how long ago, so the core stays on what is closed now, not why. The reader could reasonably object that they are not shut down, only careful — the noticing ask survives that, since looking at what is already open does not require agreeing with me. The sentence that serves me more than them is any hint that staying sealed is safe; I cut it, because the ask is to look without demanding anything change.
